title: The Day of the Fog Letters
skyStory: The moon has drifted into Pisces, sixty-two percent lit and dreamy, and it brought the fog with it. Pisces moons blur edges: the end of the wharf, the top of the hill, the line between a daydream and a plan. Sound carries strangely. A foghorn somewhere is trying to say something meaningful and keeps losing its place.

reading: Fog sits around the cabin like a wool blanket and muffles everything, including, for once, your to-do list. You will not be able to see the whole day from the porch. Good. Do the next visible thing, then the next, and let the rest stay in the mist where it belongs.

Today you are the oar. Somebody close to you is mid-crossing, and the help they need is not advice. It is steady rowing: showing up, the same time, the same warmth, no speeches. Life Path 3 will itch to give a talk. Hand over a warm mug instead. Rowing quietly is the loudest thing you can do.
joel.mission: Send Nancy a picture of something blurry and beautiful, without any explanation at all.
joel.omen: A porch light glowing through fog. You are visible to the people who need you, even when you feel hidden.

reading: Fog on the water, and the [[Six of Swords]] is pushing off from the shore again. The crossing is not finished, but today you can see a little further than last week. A shape on the far side is starting to look familiar, like a cabin with its chimney smoking.

You do not have to row hard today. Pisces wants you to drift a little, trust the current, and notice what floats by. Around 10:20 am an old memory will surface, something funny you had forgotten. Tell it to someone. Stories are how you steer through fog. Joel, on the far bank, is holding up a lantern too, very badly, slightly upside down.
nancy.mission: Write a two-line note to future-you, seal it in an envelope, and date it for the solstice.
nancy.omen: A foghorn or a distant train, sounding exactly twice. Someone on the far shore is calling your name, kindly.

together.text: Tonight, each of you light something small, a candle or a lamp, and put it in a window that faces the other's direction. Text a photo. Two little lights across the fog, showing each other the way home. The foghorn approves, at length.
